description: The city's requests (ARCHITECTURE decision 183, schema 72). Home (1, 1,500 trips a day), Work (2, 800) and Far (3, 300) on line Main with a train, one cell of 1,200 residents within 800 m of all three. Off, there are none and acceptRequest is cityRequestsNotEnabled. A managed company turns them on with seed 7: month 0's kinds sorted by FNV-1a of '7|requests.0.order.<kind>' give population first, then station riders; no settlement of 3,000, no day carried, no freight, no sights. Population picks Far (roll of '7|requests.0.population' over stations 1-3): 1,200 -> ceil(1.2 x) 1,440 residents in 120 days, $100 a resident more is below the $1,000,000 floor. Station riders picks Work (Home and Work have 500 or more): 800 -> 1,120 trips in 60 days, $40 x 320 below the $200,000 floor. One star of trust holds one request: the second is cityRequestLimitReached (limit 1); request 9 is unknownCityRequest. The land grows to 1,440 residents and the next midnight meets the first: owed $1,000,000, two stars, so the second can be taken on on day 1. The midnight that begins day 30 pays it (a monthlySubsidy row at minute 43,199, booked to day 29) and draws month 1's offers: Home's riders and Far's residents again, 1,440 -> 1,728 (Work's riders are in hand, so not asked again). Every number is worked out in tools/golden-checks/city_requests.py from the rules, not from the Swift code.
